subject: MAP: Acceptance criteria and region/mode locus for Pilot
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Elisa Moreno <elisa.moreno@caregrid.health>
Date: Tue, May 18, 2027 at 9:12 AM PDT
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Subject: Pilot MAP + region constraints

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our leadership wants a short mutual action plan (MAP) that captures acceptance criteria, timelines, and the hosting options we should evaluate (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Important constraint: CareGrid will handle PHI for a subset of calls in the pilot, so anything that touches PHI must be hosted in either our EU private environment or a Redwood Private deployment in our VPC.

Can you send a draft MAP and a short comparison that includes:
- suggested acceptance gates for the pilot (latency, throughput, cost targets)
- a proposed timeline to move from POC to pilot to prod (30/60/90-day view)
- operational owners for each lane (Redwood + CareGrid)
- pricing delta and typical lead times for Dedicated/Private options

We'd also like to lock a pilot decision by June 7.

Elisa
VP Product, CareGrid Health

---

On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 10:05 AM PDT karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:

Elisa / CareGrid team —

Appreciate the clear constraints — PHI requirement drives the region/mode conversation, and we'll capture that in the MAP. I attached a first-pass MAP (20270518-CareGrid-MAP-v1.pdf) and a short cost delta sheet (redwood-pricing-grid-q2.csv). Key highlights up front:

- Recommendation: Two-track approach for pilot
  1) Non-PHI traffic on Redwood Hosted (fastest time-to-value) with prefix caching enabled.
  2) PHI traffic (subset endpoints) in a Redwood Private deployment inside CareGrid's EU VPC, or an equivalent Private deployment we manage in EU — legal/times/cost differ.

- Acceptance gates (proposal):
  * Latency P95 <= 250ms for non-PHI flows on Hosted; P95 <= 350ms for PHI flows on Private (network overhead expected).
  * Throughput: sustained 150 rps across the pilot footprint with spikes to 400 rps for 10-minute windows.
  * Quality: end-to-end eval set BLEU/ROUGE-like pass rate > 92% (per CareGrid eval kit).

- Timeline (high level):
  * Week 0-2: finalize MAP, security checklist, and SOW.
  * Week 3-6: staging + acceptance tests (split traffic).
  * Week 7-12: pilot run, monitoring + ramp.

- Lead times: Dedicated pool provisioning ~3–4 weeks after signed order; Private (VPC-install) ~6–8 weeks depending on customer infra readiness and legal review.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm the legal / KMS ask? Grace — can your team validate the P95 targets are reasonable with our current kernel optimizations and KV caching? Priyom, I dropped a note about ops staffing for Dedicated.

Attachments: 20270518-CareGrid-MAP-v1.pdf; redwood-pricing-grid-q2.csv

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

---

On Wed, May 19, 2027 at 08:42 AM PDT Elisa Moreno <elisa.moreno@caregrid.health> wrote:

Karthik —

Quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the MAP draft:
- We cannot host PHI in Redwood Hosted under any circumstance.
- We prefer Redwood Private inside our EU VPC for PHI, but if that is operationally infeasible within the 6–8 week window, we may accept a managed Private instance hosted in Redwood EU region provided contractual assurances (KMS where keys never leave EU, SOC2 + audit log cadence).
- Procurement wants an explicit line item for the Dedicated vs Private variance in the SOW.

Can you add a short paragraph in the MAP that explains the fallback policy if Private cannot be ready by pilot start (i.e., tokenization/proxying non-PHI to Hosted, or synthetic/obfuscated PHI flows)?

Elisa

---

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 11:30 AM PDT laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:

Karthik / team —

Legal and compliance notes (high level):
- For EU PHI we need either: customer-managed KMS in the EU or a dedicated HSM-backed key material with strict egress controls; confirm which CareGrid prefers.
- Audit log retention: procurement asked for 12 months minimum; we can offer 12/24/36 tiers as add-ons.
- Data residency clause: add explicit clause that model weights and training telemetry do not contain PHI; inference logs that contain PHI must be stored only in the EU boundary for the Private lane.

I'll draft the paragraph for the fallback policy and attach a minimal security checklist. I referenced security-evidence-summary.zip for the team.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference

Attachment: security-evidence-summary.zip

---

On Mon, May 24, 2027 at 09:08 AM PDT priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:

Ops / infra check —

Based on the pilot sizing in the MAP (150 rps sustained), ops notes:
- Dedicated US pool: we can reserve a 4-GPU pool and hit the throughput target with autoscale headroom; typical cost delta ~ +35% vs Hosted per million tokens (see pricing sheet).
- Private (EU VPC install): engineering install window depends on CareGrid network readiness. If CareGrid already has an approved peering and a route to our installer VM, we can complete install in ~4 weeks; otherwise plan for ~6–8 weeks with firewall/infra changes.
- Fallback: we can run a tokenization/proxy in front of Hosted to keep PHI out of Hosted if Private is delayed, but that requires CareGrid to own the tokenization key and process (we'll provide an SDK).

@Grace: small ask — if we enable prefix KV caching and bump batch size by 1.5x are we still within the P95 targets for non-PHI hosted flows?

Priyom
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

---

On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 4:45 PM PDT karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:

Team / Elisa —

Summary and proposed lane decision to present to CareGrid execs on Friday (June 4):

Proposed MAP-driven lane decision (pilot):
1) Non-PHI — Redwood Hosted (fast start)
   - Acceptance gates: P95 <= 250ms, throughput sustain 150 rps.
   - Owner: Redwood (ops + solutions), CareGrid product for eval sets.
2) PHI — Redwood Private inside CareGrid EU VPC (preferred) OR managed Redwood Private in EU with customer-managed KMS (fallback).
   - Acceptance gates: P95 <= 350ms, audit logs retained 12 months by default.
   - Owner: CareGrid infra + Redwood install team.
3) Contingency (if Private not ready by pilot): tokenization/proxy pattern with PHI-stripping on-prem + non-PHI to Hosted for feature ramp.

Operational asks to finalize MAP and sign SOW by June 7:
- CareGrid to confirm KMS preference (customer-managed vs Redwood HSM) and VPC peering window.
- Procurement to confirm PO timeline and which pricing tier (Dedicated vs Private add-on).
- Redwood to provide a final SOW with explicit line items and the fallback paragraph (Laura will attach).

I'll present this recommendation on Friday and include the security checklist and cost delta table. If this looks good, Elisa please confirm and we'll convert the MAP v1 -> v1.1 and circulate a DocuSign prefill.

Thanks all,
Karthik

Attachments referenced: 20270518-CareGrid-MAP-v1.pdf; security-evidence-summary.zip; redwood-pricing-grid-q2.csv
